gates.claim: landenCombo_ofReal_eq_zero AS STATED: Li2(t) + Li2(t/(t-1)) + log(1-t)^2/2 = 0 for every real t < 0. 200 points from -0.05 to -10. This is the Lean theorem's exact content, not a nearby identity

THE PINNING THE PROOF USES: the combination tends to 0 as t -> 0-, over eight decades. The Lean proof takes the constant from the endpoint 0 (where cLiTwoExt_zero and log 1 = 0 make every term vanish) and `Ico t 0` excludes the one point where the derivative hypotheses fail. If this limit were any nonzero constant the theorem would be FALSE, not merely unproved

WHY THE BASE POINT IS 0 AND NOT -1, checked rather than asserted. At z = -1 the combination is Li2(-1) + Li2(1/2) + log(2)^2/2. Each of the three pieces is INDIVIDUALLY NONZERO, so pinning there genuinely needs Li2(1/2) = pi^2/12 - log(2)^2/2 -- a value Mathlib does not have (it has hasSum_zeta_two only). They cancel to 0 exactly, which is why the identity holds; but the cancellation is not available without the special value. Pinning at 0 needs no value at all

NON-VACUITY: all six hypotheses of hasDerivAt_landenCombo hold SIMULTANEOUSLY at every one of the 200 sampled points. This is the gate class that caught correction 6 in PR #4701, where a slitPlane hypothesis failed at all 199 arc points and made its theorem vacuous. Type-checking would never have found it

ADVERSARIAL ON THE REGIME: for t > 1 the same combination is NOT zero, so the restriction to t < 0 is load-bearing rather than a convenience. t = 2.24698 is included deliberately -- it is w_1, the one argument `extended_sum` uses that lies in the INVERSION regime, and it is exactly the value this theorem does not reach. A proof that appeared to cover it would be wrong

CHECKED OFF THE CONFIGURATION IT WILL BE USED ON: the identity also holds at complex points off the real axis, where the Lean theorem says nothing. If it held ONLY on the negative reals that would signal the real-restriction had smuggled something in; it does not

SCOPE, named per argument rather than left in prose. Of the six arguments `extended_sum` uses, this theorem reaches exactly those that are NEGATIVE -- the Landen regime of `extend`. The non-negative ones are untouched: those in [0,1] need nothing (the series already agrees), and w_1 = 2.24698 needs the INVERSION leg, which is still open and is the sharper of the two
gates.still_open: the inversion leg for x > 1: x > 1 lies ON cLiTwoExt's cut (notCut excludes real x >= 1), so it needs a boundary value from off the cut, not a constant of integration

verdict.closed_this_round: the Landen leg of qou-rstq item 4, on the negative reals. Route 33 G5 named the connectedness step as the only thing missing from this leg; it is now proved, sorry-free and lake-verified, with the constant pinned at the limit t -> 0- so that no special value of Li2 is needed.
verdict.still_open: the INVERSION leg (x > 1), unchanged and still the sharper of the two. Exactly one of the six arguments needs it, w_1 = 2.24698, and it cannot be avoided. Also unchanged: identifying the corpus's PIECEWISE `extend` with Re of the analytic Rogers L still needs the real-part bookkeeping on top of these identities.
verdict.not_claimed: this does NOT close qou-rstq item 4, and does not touch the sum rule. It closes one of the two analytic legs that item rests on.
